title: pi-dispatch
brief: Runs the pi coding agent as a self-hosted background service: triggered on demand, on a cron schedule, or by GitHub/GitLab issues, comments, and pull/merge requests, each job executing in a locked-down ephemeral container with a durable queue. It enforces per-job/daily/weekly/monthly spend caps before a single token is spent, and ships a live admin panel with run history, cost insights, and per-trigger spend analytics; MIT-licensed. Note: the bare npm name `pi-dispatch` belongs to an unrelated package — the scoped `@edgehero/pi-dispatch` is the correct install.
details: pi-dispatch (edgehero/pi-dispatch, MIT) runs the open-source pi coding agent as a self-hosted background service instead of an interactive terminal session. Jobs start from a cron schedule, the CLI, or forge events (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Azure DevOps — e.g. an issue labeled ai or an @pi comment), and each job executes inside its own locked-down Docker or Podman container (non-root, all Linux capabilities dropped, deleted afterward), which acts as the permission system pi itself lacks. It adds the operational layer pi is missing: a durable Valkey-backed queue, spend limits enforced before anything is spent (per-job turn limits plus daily, weekly, monthly, and per-repo caps), run history with per-flow cost insights, and a live /dispatch admin panel showing queue state, spend meters, triggers, and pause windows. It reuses your repo's existing .pi/ setup (skills and persona) so the agent follows your conventions, supports multi-stage workflows and third-party pi extensions, and deliberately never merges anything itself — what comes back is a pull request you review. Setup is guided via pi install npm:@edgehero/pi-dispatch-admin or npx @edgehero/pi-dispatch up on any machine with Node 22+ and a container runtime.
